full_judgment: 8. In view of the circumstances as noted above, it would not be correct to say that the proceeding for amalgamation and consolidation of holdings under sections 116 and 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was initiated suo motu without having any basis. In the auction sale P.S. Plot No. 108 as appearing appertained to new P.S. Khatian No. 18 was sold. It is admitted that plot No. 108 previously appertained to khatian No. 14, and in its 16 annas belonged to H.E. Percival. So separation of plot No.108 from khatian No. 14 and its amalgamation in khatian No. 18, could not prejudice the pre-emptors who claimed to be a co- sharer in khatian No. 14 on the basis of their purchase from H.E. Percival. Apart from that there is a presumption under the law that all official acts are presumed to have been rightly and regularly done.
